_note: Fixed before the remedy was built. Each rule carries the verdict a careful reader would reach about THIS repository, justified independently of any checker. `expect` is what the checker must produce: 'held', 'broken', or 'undecided'. Undecided is correct for rules no source inspection can settle — claiming otherwise is the failure this guards against.

cases.rule: Each repository must correspond to exactly one knowledge base. A single KB must not be shared across repositories.
cases.because: corpus_id() keys by repository; tests pin one-repo-one-KB and two-repos-two-KBs

cases.rule: There must be one shared .env file for the v3 family, not one .env per service.
cases.because: no .env exists inside vesta; the family's single .env is at v3/

cases.rule: langextract is either fully present as a dependency or fully absent; there is no partial or conditional use.
cases.because: vesta does not depend on langextract at all, so the rule is trivially honoured here

cases.rule: The tool must be language-agnostic; it must not be specific to Python repositories.
cases.because: dynamic.py SOURCE and rules sifting cover a fixed suffix list; resolve.py SERVERS is a fixed table. Real, and the user raised it directly.
cases.outcome: NOT MET. The checker returns undecided and its reason is defensible: 'is language-agnostic' is a property of the tool, and no pattern over source establishes it. The same intent stated as a property of the source — 'must not hardcode a list of languages or file suffixes' — is checked correctly and finds 9 real sites at vesta/resolve.py:86-98. The fixture was left as written rather than restated, because rewording a case after seeing the result is how a standard stops being one.

cases.rule: Every source file must carry a module docstring explaining what it is for.
cases.because: every vesta/*.py opens with a docstring; verifiable by reading the first lines

cases.rule: No module may import the sidecar, so that the CLI works without the mcp package installed.
cases.because: cli.py imports THEORY_DIR from structure, not sidecar; this was fixed earlier for exactly this reason

cases.rule: Quality, precision and correctness take priority over latency optimisation.
cases.because: a priority between competing values; no source inspection settles it

cases.rule: The prompt implementation must be tested against a live provider before being considered complete.
cases.because: a claim about what was run, not about what the source says

cases.rule: Users must be able to select a specific ontology when creating a run.
cases.because: a product capability claim about a UI this repository does not contain

_result: 8 of 9 as written, stable across three runs.
